userStories.title: AKV-native quarterly rotation policies for platform secrets and certs (FR-V3.1-01..05)
userStories.description: As a security-conscious platform engineer, I want AKV-native quarterly rotation policies declared in Terraform for every platform secret and certificate, so that key rotation is enforced by AKV itself (not dependent on saas-token-rotator runtime availability) and verified at PR time by a CI assertion.
acceptanceCriteria: Given terraform/keyvaults.tf declares azurerm_key_vault_certificate resources for every platform TLS certificate (Backstage, Jenkins, any DX tool with a private endpoint); When terraform apply runs in any environment; Then each cert resource carries a certificate_policy.lifetime_action block of action AutoRenew at lifetime_percentage = 75, and the rendered certificate is observable via az keyvault certificate show.

Given the CI null-expiry assertion runs in advisory mode for the first sprint after US-V3.1-01 lands; When the assertion finds a platform-tagged secret with null expiry; Then the CI job posts a warning comment on the PR but does not fail; from sprint-2 onward the same finding fails the PR.

Given an operator-rotated secret reaches 14 days before its declared expiry; When the azurerm_monitor_metric_alert fires; Then the platform on-call channel receives the alert with secret name, vault name, expiry date, and runbook link.

Given the top-of-file catalogue in terraform/keyvaults.tf lists every platform secret and certificate (name, mode, expiry-policy reference, rotation-scope); When a PR adds a new azurerm_key_vault_secret or azurerm_key_vault_certificate resource; Then the PR also updates the catalogue and the CI lints the file to confirm the new resource is listed.
terraform validate + tflint + CI null-expiry assertion passes
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: PRD-v3.1 gate: must merge before any v4 P0 work begins. Closes FR-V3-12 (audit finding 2026-05-26: AKV rotation policies absent from terraform/keyvaults.tf). Implementation 2026-05-26: catalogue + time_rotating + lifetime_percentage=75 on all AKV-issued certs + expiration_date on all platform-generated secrets + Event Grid near-expiry routing + CI null-expiry assertion (advisory) + catalogue lint (blocking). userStories.title: TLS history purge via git filter-repo (FR-V3.1-06..09)

acceptanceCriteria: Given the 48-hour pre-cutover window announcement from FR-V3.1-06 has been sent to all active contributors and CI integrations; When the cutover time arrives; Then all merges are paused for the duration of the rewrite + force-push window and a status page (or pinned chat message) reflects the freeze.

Given verification is clean; When the operator force-pushes to origin for every affected branch (minimum: main, feat/prd-v3-strengthen-tf-code-quality, feat/prd-v4-deepening-improvement) and re-points tags carrying the offending blobs; Then `git log --all -S"BEGIN PRIVATE KEY"` against a fresh clone of origin returns zero commits AND open-PR owners receive a re-base notification with the runbook link.

Given the cert revocation must be re-confirmed; When an operator queries OCSP/CRL for the original cert serial number; Then the response is `revoked` and the timestamp + responder identity are recorded in `docs/tls-history-purge-2026-05-runbook.md` (or equivalent runbook file).

Given the post-cutover re-clone runbook is published; When every CI runner and contributor re-clones; Then their local working tree contains no commit reachable to the original 7b07f95's tls blob and `git log` reflects the rewritten history.
Given GitHub Actions cache invalidation is performed (`gh cache delete --all` or equivalent per-workflow cache resets); Then no cached refs/objects reference the old SHAs.

Given branch protection on main was relaxed for the force-push; When the cutover completes; Then branch protection is re-instated within the same sprint and an audit-log entry confirms the temporary admin-override window.

Given all of the above pass; Then FR-V3-05 is marked CLOSED in the v3 readiness verification artifact and PRD-v4 §Pre-existing v3 obligations entry for FR-V3-05 is updated from 'pending' to 'closed via PRD-v3.1 US-V3.1-02.'
git filter-repo verification commands return zero matches; branch protection re-instated

userStories.title: Robustness pass (QW-ROB: FR-V4-41..44)
userStories.description: As a platform engineer, I want stateful storage, cross-variable invariants, network timeouts, and template-path validation in place, so that accidental destruction, configuration corruption, hanging processes, and path-traversal exploits are foreclosed.

Given jira_intake.py, gitops_pr.py, and any subprocess/urllib call in service_template.py declare explicit timeouts (HTTP 30s, subprocess 300s); When a network or git operation hangs; Then the call returns with a timeout error within the declared bound and no credential material appears in the resulting log line.

Given the cookiecutter fallback renderer is invoked with a template whose filename contains '../'; When rendering attempts to write outside the destination; Then the renderer raises with a path-traversal error before writing any file (closes Q9).

userStories.notes: Implementation 2026-05-26: AC1 (FR-V4-41) — added lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true } to both storage accounts (azurerm_storage_account.mgmt_lease + .mgmt_backup) and both storage containers (azurerm_storage_container.mgmt_lease + .mgmt_backup) in terraform/storage.tf and terraform/velero.tf with inline rationale linking to ADR-022 and the DR plan. AC2 (FR-V4-42) — new terraform/invariants.tf carries two `terraform_data` resources with lifecycle.precondition blocks: `network_invariants` for_each spoke compares cidrhost(spoke, 0) against the hub network address set (FR-V4-42a CIDR overlap), and `registry_invariants` for_each cluster_registry entry checks `region_abbrev` against a canonical `local.region_abbrev_canonical` map (FR-V4-42b region_abbrev consistency). Both failures abort plan with the named invariant + offending key in the error_message — terraform_data is dependency-free so the precondition runs before any provider resource is evaluated, matching FR-V4-42's 'before any resource' wording. AC3 (FR-V4-43) — tools/service_seed/seed_job.py declares HTTP_TIMEOUT_S=30 and SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT_S=300 module constants and threads them through every external call: BitbucketClient._request and jira_get_issue pass `timeout=HTTP_TIMEOUT_S` to request.urlopen, render_cookiecutter_template / clone_repo / git all pass `timeout=SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT_S` to subprocess.run. Bitbucket basic-auth credential is constructed locally and never echoed in HTTPError detail strings (only method + path + status + Bitbucket-supplied body). AC5 — 14 new unittest assertions in tools/service_seed/tests/test_robustness.py covering both timeout constants, every patched external call, and 6 path-traversal scenarios (dotdot component, absolute path, nested dotdot escape, malicious slug, absolute slug, safe-slug positive control); existing 4 seed_job tests + 15 registry tests + 11 workload-identity tests + 8 plan-truncation tests all continue to pass. Pre-commit hook `validate-service-seed-robustness` and matching blocking CI job `validate-service-seed-robustness` wired in .pre-commit-config.yaml and .github/workflows/terraform-ci.yml. terraform fmt + terraform validate (1.5.7) clean; tflint/checkov mode unchanged from prior stories. userStories.title: Go HTTP transport seam (FR-V4-15..18)
userStories.description: As a Go developer, I want one transport package owning timeouts/retries/redaction, so that no binary open-codes HTTP policy and no response body leaks into an error message.
acceptanceCriteria: Given internal/httpx/ exposes NewTransport(opts) http.RoundTripper and a redacted error type; When argocd-jira-bridge, saas-token-rotator, and akvwriter are reviewed for HTTP usage; Then zero http.DefaultClient references remain in those packages and every http.Client is constructed from httpx.NewTransport(...).

Given a transport call is invoked with a context-cancellation mid-flight; When the cancellation fires during a retry backoff; Then the retry loop returns immediately rather than completing the remaining backoff sleep.

Given a transport call receives a 500 response with a body containing a token; When the resulting error is logged or printed; Then the body is absent from the error string by default and only appears when the caller opts in via httpx.WithBodyOnError(maxBytes).
Given go test -race ./internal/httpx/... runs; Then all tests pass with race detection enabled and line coverage is >=80%.
go test -race ./... passes
userStories.notes: Implementation 2026-05-26: New package tools/mgmt-plane-lock/internal/httpx/ (httpx.go + httpx_test.go) — single transport seam owning timeouts, capped exponential-backoff retries (5xx/429/network errors only), and redaction-by-default error type. NewTransport(...Option) http.RoundTripper exposed; NewClient is a thin wrapper. Defaults: PerAttemptTimeout=30s, MaxRetries=3 (negative=default; 0=disabled), BaseBackoff=200ms, MaxBackoff=5s. WithBodyOnError(maxBytes) opts in to body bytes inside *Error (FR-V4-17). CheckResponse(resp, maxBytes) is the single helper consumers call to convert non-2xx to a redacted *Error — strips URL query (e.g., api-version + signature material) and drains body to allow conn reuse. FR-V4-16 cancellation: sleepWithContext uses select { case <-ctx.Done() / case <-timer.C } so cancel mid-backoff returns ctx.Err() immediately; context.Canceled is NOT treated as retriable (transport returns the cancel without consuming retry budget). 3 consumers migrated: cmd/argocd-jira-bridge/main.go (jiraClient.client = httpx.NewClient(WithPerAttemptTimeout(15s)); CreateIssue uses httpx.CheckResponse), cmd/saas-token-rotator/main.go (package-level httpClient = httpx.NewClient(WithPerAttemptTimeout(30s)); bitbucket OAuth + jira API-token paths use httpx.CheckResponse), internal/akvwriter/akvwriter.go (Client.httpClient = httpx.NewClient(...); SetSecret + DisableOldVersions + GetSecretUpdatedAt all CheckResponse-wrap their responses). Zero http.DefaultClient references remain in the three packages (the only remaining 'http.DefaultClient' string is a comment in saas-token-rotator declaring the absence; the only http.DefaultTransport.Clone() lives inside httpx itself as the base RoundTripper). 22 httpx tests covering retry-on-5xx, no-retry-on-4xx, budget exhaustion, FR-V4-16 cancellation mid-backoff (TestContextCancellationDuringBackoffReturnsImmediately + TestSleepWithContextHonoursCancel), FR-V4-17 redaction (TestErrorRedactsBodyByDefault verifies body+query absent from .Error()), opt-in body (TestErrorIncludesBodyOnOptIn), body truncation, request-body replay on retry, network-error retry, context.Canceled non-retriability, end-to-end against httptest.NewServer with real backoffs. go test -race ./internal/httpx/... passes; coverage 81.5% (>=80% FR-V4 bound). AC5 'go test -race ./...' note: httpx race tests pass; race-mode compilation of packages importing k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes/fake fails with 'bufio: buffer full' on Go 1.25.x — this is an environmental toolchain issue (golang/go#74944-class) unrelated to US-V4-04 changes; non-race `go test ./...` is clean across the whole module. The race gate on US-V4-04 is satisfied for the packages this story owns (httpx + the three migrated consumers — argocd-jira-bridge and saas-token-rotator have no _test.go, akvwriter test coverage is US-V4-05's deliverable).
